key_insights: Before listing a recommender's contact information on an application, confirm with them directly that they are willing to write the letter
When asking, state who you are, why you're requesting the letter, why the program is your top choice, and how the recommender helped prepare you
Give recommenders a firm submission deadline earlier than the actual application deadline (e.g., three weeks early) to allow time for follow-up
Ask people who taught or supervised you for more than one class or engagement, and who are in a relevant field
If a program requires one academic and one professional letter, be careful not to submit two of the same type
specific_numbers_or_facts: Example given by the speaker: if the application deadline is May 1, request the letter be submitted by April 10
notable_or_distinctive: generic advice; off-scope for this undergraduate-admissions knowledge base since it is explicitly a graduate school admissions video
reliability_notes: OFF-SCOPE: this is graduate admissions content (Kutztown University graduate admissions director), not US undergraduate admissions, so relevance is marked low despite otherwise clear and credible advice.
